newsitem.title: USA: Oakley sees Q4 EPS, sales below consensus.
newsitem.headline: Oakley sees Q4 EPS, sales below consensus.

text.p: Oakley Inc said a reduction in business with customer Sunglass Hut International Inc in the fourth quarter will cause Oakley's earnings per share to be below the consensus analyst estimate of $0.16 per share.
Net sales for the quarter are expected to be relatively flat compared with the 1995 fourth quarter, and earnings per share are expected to fall about 30 percent, it said.
Sales and earnings are also expected to be negatively affected by the timing of new product introductions, which have only begun to benefit sales late in the quarter.

Sunglass Hut recently requested Oakley delay shipment of November orders and Oakley does not expect Sunglass Hut to take delivery on remaining pending fourth quarter orders, based on discussions and inventory levels, it said.

But it does not expect orders for Oakley's new products to be reduced or delayed by Sunglass Hut. "While we are disappointed with the short-term impact on our results, we believe the reduction in shipments to Sunglass Hut in the fourth quarter is in Oakley's best interest long-term," said Mike Parnell, chief executive officer of Oakley, who said he is confident in the company's 1997 outlook.
